sanskrit: ulmukaṃ bhrāmayaṃs tūrṇaṃ pāṇḍavaś carma cottamam vyapovāha śarāṃs tasya sarvān eva dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: Swiftly whirling the firebrand and raising his excellent shield, Dhanañjaya — the Pāṇḍava — deflected every single arrow of his.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca bibhīṣikaiṣā gandharva nāstrajñeṣu prayujyate astrajñeṣu prayuktaiṣā phenavat pravilīyate
english: Arjuna said: O gandharva, this terror of yours is not deployed against those who know the science of weapons; when directed at those who do know it, it dissolves like foam.

sanskrit: mānuṣān ati gandharvān sarvān gandharva lakṣaye tasmād astreṇa divyena yotsye 'haṃ na tu māyayā
english: I regard all gandharvas as surpassing ordinary men, O gandharva; therefore I shall fight with a divine weapon, and not with illusion.

sanskrit: purāstram idam āgneyaṃ prādāt kila bṛhaspatiḥ bharadvājasya gandharva guruputraḥ śatakratoḥ
english: Long ago, O gandharva, Bṛhaspati — son of the guru of Śatakratu — bestowed this fire weapon upon Bharadvaja.

sanskrit: bharadvājād agniveśyo agniveśyād gurur mama sa tv idaṃ mahyam adadād droṇo brāhmaṇasattamaḥ
english: From Bharadvaja it passed to Agnivesha, and from Agnivesha to my guru; that foremost of brahmanas, Droṇa, gave it to me.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ity uktvā pāṇḍavaḥ kruddho gandharvāya mumoca ha pradīptam astram āgneyaṃ dadāhāsya rathaṃ tu tat
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken thus, the Pāṇḍava, filled with wrath, released the blazing fire weapon at the gandharva, and it set his chariot ablaze.

sanskrit: virathaṃ viplutaṃ taṃ tu sa gandharvaṃ mahābalam astratejaḥpramūḍhaṃ ca prapatantam avāṅmukham
english: That mighty gandharva was left without a chariot, utterly undone, bewildered by the brilliance of the weapon, and fell forward face downward.

sanskrit: śiroruheṣu jagrāha mālyavatsu dhanaṃjayaḥ bhrātṝn prati cakarṣātha so 'strapātād acetasam
english: Dhanañjaya seized him by his garlanded hair and dragged him — rendered senseless by the fall of the weapon — toward his brothers.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiraṃ tasya bhāryā prapede śaraṇārthinī nāmnā kumbhīnasī nāma patitrāṇam abhīpsatī
english: His wife, named Kumbhīnasī, seeking refuge and desiring to save her husband, threw herself before Yudhiṣṭhira as a suppliant.

sanskrit: gandharvy uvāca trāhi tvaṃ māṃ mahārāja patiṃ cemaṃ vimuñca me gandharvīṃ śaraṇaṃ prāptāṃ nāmnā kumbīnasīṃ prabho
english: The gandharva woman said: Save me, O great king, and release this husband of mine! I am a gandharva woman who has come to you for refuge — I am named Kumbhīnasī, O lord.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca yuddhe jitaṃ yaśohīnaṃ strīnātham aparākramam ko nu hanyād ripuṃ tvādṛṅ muñcemaṃ ripusūdana
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Who indeed would slay an enemy who has been conquered in battle, stripped of glory, whose wife is his master, and who is no longer a warrior? O slayer of foes, release him.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca aṅgemaṃ pratipadyasva gaccha gandharva mā śucaḥ pradiśaty abhayaṃ te 'dya kururājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Arjuna said: Take him back, O gandharva woman — go and do not grieve. The Kuru king Yudhiṣṭhira grants you safety today.

sanskrit: gandharva uvāca jito 'haṃ pūrvakaṃ nāma muñcāmy aṅgāraparṇatām na ca ślāghe balenādya na nāmnā janasaṃsadi
english: The gandharva said: I have been defeated; I relinquish my former name Aṅgāraparṇa. Henceforth I shall not boast of my strength or my name in any gathering of people.

sanskrit: sādhv imaṃ labdhavāṃl lābhaṃ yo 'haṃ divyāstradhāriṇam gāndharvyā māyayā yoddhum icchāmi vayasā varam
english: It is well indeed that I have gained this gain — that I, who wished to fight with gandharva illusion against one who wields divine weapons and is superior to me in age and valor.

sanskrit: astrāgninā vicitro 'yaṃ dagdho me ratha uttamaḥ so 'haṃ citraratho bhūtvā nāmnā dagdharatho 'bhavam
english: My magnificent chariot has been burned by the fire of that weapon; I who was once Chitraratha have now become Dagdharatha — the one with the burnt chariot — in name.

sanskrit: saṃbhṛtā caiva vidyeyaṃ tapaseha purā mayā nivedayiṣye tām adya prāṇadāyā mahātmane
english: This knowledge was gathered by me through austerities long ago; today I shall present it to this great-souled one who has given me back my life.

sanskrit: saṃstambhitaṃ hi tarasā jitaṃ śaraṇam āgatam yo 'riṃ saṃyojayet prāṇaiḥ kalyāṇaṃ kiṃ na so 'rhati
english: He who reunites with life an enemy who was overpowered by force, defeated, and has come seeking refuge — does he not deserve every good fortune?

sanskrit: cakṣuṣī nāma vidyeyaṃ yāṃ somāya dadau manuḥ dadau sa viśvāvasave mahyaṃ viśvāvasur dadau
english: This knowledge is called Chakshushi — that which Manu gave to Soma; Soma gave it to Viśvāvasu, and Viśvāvasu gave it to me.

sanskrit: seyaṃ kāpuruṣaṃ prāptā gurudattā praṇaśyati āgamo 'syā mayā prokto vīryaṃ pratinibodha me
english: This guru-given knowledge, if it reaches a coward, is lost; I have described its origin — now hear from me its power.

sanskrit: yac cakṣuṣā draṣṭum icchet triṣu lokeṣu kiṃ cana tat paśyed yādṛśaṃ cecchet tādṛṣaṃ draṣṭum arhati
english: Whatever one wishes to see with the eye in the three worlds, one can see it; and in whatever form one wishes to see it, one is able to behold it in that very form.

sanskrit: samānapadye ṣaṇmāsān sthito vidyāṃ labhed imām anuneṣyāmy ahaṃ vidyāṃ svayaṃ tubhyaṃ vrate kṛte
english: One who remains established in the vow for six months will obtain this knowledge; I myself will conduct this knowledge to you once the vow is observed.

sanskrit: vidyayā hy anayā rājan vayaṃ nṛbhyo viśeṣitāḥ aviśiṣṭāś ca devānām anubhāvapravartitāḥ
english: By this knowledge, O king, we gandharvas are distinguished above men, yet we fall short of the gods, being moved by their power.

sanskrit: gandharvajānām aśvānām ahaṃ puruṣasattama bhrātṛbhyas tava pañcabhyaḥ pṛthag dātā śataṃ śatam
english: I shall give, O best of men, one hundred horses born of gandharvas each separately to your five brothers — a hundred for each.

sanskrit: devagandharvavāhās te divyagandhā manogamāḥ kṣīṇāḥ kṣīṇā bhavanty ete na hīyante ca raṃhasaḥ
english: These are the mounts of the gods and gandharvas, of divine fragrance, traveling at the speed of thought; though they may tire and tire again, their swiftness never diminishes.

sanskrit: purā kṛtaṃ mahendrasya vajraṃ vṛtranibarhaṇe daśadhā śatadhā caiva tac chīrṇaṃ vṛtramūrdhani
english: Long ago, the thunderbolt of Mahendra, fashioned for the slaying of Vṛtra, was shattered tenfold and a hundredfold upon the head of Vṛtra.

sanskrit: tato bhāgīkṛto devair vajrabhāga upāsyate loke yat sādhanaṃ kiṃ cit sā vai vajratanuḥ smṛtā
english: Those portions were then distributed among the gods, and the share of the thunderbolt is worshipped in the world; whatever in the world serves as a means of power — that is said to be the body of the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: vajrapāṇir brāhmaṇaḥ syāt kṣatraṃ vajrarathaṃ smṛtam vaiśyā vai dānavajrāś ca karmavajrā yavīyasaḥ
english: A brahmin is the thunderbolt in the hand; the kshatriya is said to be the thunderbolt of the chariot; the vaishyas are the thunderbolt of giving, and the youngest class the thunderbolt of action.

sanskrit: vajraṃ kṣatrasya vājino avadhyā vājinaḥ smṛtāḥ rathāṅgaṃ vaḍavā sūte sūtāś cāśveṣu ye matāḥ
english: Horses are the thunderbolt of the kshatriya; horses are declared to be inviolable; a mare gives birth to the wheel of the chariot, and those considered chariot-drivers are among horses.

sanskrit: kāmavarṇāḥ kāmajavāḥ kāmataḥ samupasthitāḥ ime gandharvajāḥ kāmaṃ pūrayiṣyanti te hayāḥ
english: Of any color one desires, born as one desires, appearing at one's will — these horses born of gandharvas will fulfill your every wish.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca yadi prītena vā dattaṃ saṃśaye jīvitasya vā vidyā vittaṃ śrutaṃ vāpi na tad gandharva kāmaye
english: Arjuna said: Whether given out of affection or when one's life was in danger — knowledge, wealth, or learning — I do not desire that, O gandharva.

sanskrit: gandharva uvāca saṃyogo vai prītikaraḥ saṃsatsu pratidṛśyate jīvitasya pradānena prīto vidyāṃ dadāmi te
english: The gandharva said: Fellowship indeed brings joy, as is seen in all assemblies; delighted by the gift of my life, I give you this knowledge.

sanskrit: tvatto hy ahaṃ grahīṣyāmi astram āgneyam uttamam tathaiva sakhyaṃ bībhatso cirāya bharatarṣabha
english: From you I shall receive the supreme fire weapon in return, and likewise an enduring friendship, O Bībhatsu, O bull among the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca tvatto 'streṇa vṛṇomy aśvān saṃyogaḥ śāśvato 'stu nau sakhe tad brūhi gandharva yuṣmabhyo yad bhayaṃ tyajet
english: Arjuna said: In exchange for the weapon I choose the horses from you; let our union be eternal, O friend. Tell me, O gandharva, what it is that would free you from fear.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca kāraṇaṃ brūhi gandharva kiṃ tad yena sma dharṣitāḥ yānto brahmavidaḥ santaḥ sarve rātrāv ariṃdama
english: Arjuna said: Tell me the reason, O gandharva — what was it by which we were assailed — we who were traveling, knowing the Vedas, virtuous, all of us, at night, O subduer of enemies?

sanskrit: gandharva uvāca anagnayo 'nāhutayo na ca viprapuraskṛtāḥ yūyaṃ tato dharṣitāḥ stha mayā pāṇḍavanandana
english: The gandharva said: You were without fire, without offerings made into fire, and not accompanied by a brahmin in the lead — therefore you were assailed by me, O joy of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: yakṣarākṣasagandharvāḥ piśācoragamānavāḥ vistaraṃ kuruvaṃśasya śrīmataḥ kathayanti te
english: Yakṣas, rakshasas, gandharvas, pisachas, serpents, and men — all these tell at length of the glory of your illustrious Kuru lineage.

sanskrit: nāradaprabhṛtīnāṃ ca devarṣīṇāṃ mayā śrutam guṇān kathayatāṃ vīra pūrveṣāṃ tava dhīmatām
english: And from Nārada and other divine sages I have heard, O hero, them recounting the virtues of your wise forebears.

sanskrit: svayaṃ cāpi mayā dṛṣṭaś caratā sāgarāmbarām imāṃ vasumatīṃ kṛtsnāṃ prabhāvaḥ svakulasya te
english: And I myself have seen, as I wandered across this entire earth girdled by oceans, the power of your own lineage.

sanskrit: vede dhanuṣi cācāryam abhijānāmi te 'rjuna viśrutaṃ triṣu lokeṣu bhāradvājaṃ yaśasvinam
english: I recognize, O Arjuna, your teacher in the Veda and in archery — the illustrious Bharadvaja's son, renowned in the three worlds.

sanskrit: dharmaṃ vāyuṃ ca śakraṃ ca vijānāmy aśvinau tathā pāṇḍuṃ ca kuruśārdūla ṣaḍ etān kulavardhanān pitṝn etān ahaṃ pārtha devamānuṣasattamān
english: I know Dharma, Vāyu, and Śakra, likewise the Aśvins, and Pāṇḍu — these six, O tiger among Kurus, O Pārtha, these fathers, foremost among gods and men, who increased your lineage.

sanskrit: divyātmāno mahātmānaḥ sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varāḥ bhavanto bhrātaraḥ śūrāḥ sarve sucaritavratāḥ
english: You brothers are of divine nature, great-souled, the foremost of all who bear weapons, heroic, all of you observing vows of noble conduct.

sanskrit: uttamāṃ tu manobuddhiṃ bhavatāṃ bhāvitātmanām jānann api ca vaḥ pārtha kṛtavān iha dharṣaṇām
english: Yet knowing your sublime mind and intellect, O Pārtha, knowing you to be souls of disciplined spirit — I nevertheless committed this assault upon you here.

sanskrit: strīsakāśe ca kauravya na pumān kṣantum arhati dharṣaṇām ātmanaḥ paśyan bāhudraviṇam āśritaḥ
english: In the presence of women, O Kauravya, no man who relies upon the wealth of his arms ought to endure an insult to himself when he sees it.

sanskrit: naktaṃ ca balam asmākaṃ bhūya evābhivardhate yatas tato māṃ kaunteya sadāraṃ manyur āviśat
english: And at night our strength increases even further; that is why wrath came upon me together with my wife, O son of Kuntī.

sanskrit: so 'haṃ tvayeha vijitaḥ saṃkhye tāpatyavardhana yena teneha vidhinā kīrtyamānaṃ nibodha me
english: Yet I have been defeated by you here in battle, O enhancer of the lineage of Tapatī; learn from me by what means this glory is to be proclaimed.

sanskrit: brahmacaryaṃ paro dharmaḥ sa cāpi niyatas tvayi yasmāt tasmād ahaṃ pārtha raṇe 'smin vijitas tvayā
english: Brahmacharya — celibate discipline — is the supreme dharma, and that too is established in you; it is for this reason, O Pārtha, that I was conquered by you in this battle.

sanskrit: yas tu syāt kṣatriyaḥ kaś cit kāmavṛttaḥ paraṃtapa naktaṃ ca yudhi yudhyeta na sa jīvet kathaṃ cana
english: Whatever kshatriya, O scorcher of foes, is governed by desire and fights in battle at night — he cannot survive under any circumstances.

sanskrit: yas tu syāt kāmavṛtto 'pi rājā tāpatya saṃgare jayen naktaṃcarān sarvān sa purohitadhūrgataḥ
english: But a king who is even governed by desire, O descendant of Tapatī, can conquer all night-roaming beings in battle — provided he is guided by a purohita at the helm.

sanskrit: tasmāt tāpatya yat kiṃ cin nṛṇāṃ śreya ihepsitam tasmin karmaṇi yoktavyā dāntātmānaḥ purohitāḥ
english: Therefore, O descendant of Tapatī, in whatever action men here seek their highest good, self-controlled purohitas should be engaged for that undertaking.

sanskrit: vede ṣaḍaṅge niratāḥ śucayaḥ satyavādinaḥ dharmātmānaḥ kṛtātmānaḥ syur nṛpāṇāṃ purohitāḥ
english: Those who are devoted to the Veda with its six limbs, who are pure, truthful in speech, righteous in soul, and disciplined in self — such men should be the purohitas of kings.

sanskrit: jayaś ca niyato rājñaḥ svargaś ca syād anantaram yasya syād dharmavid vāgmī purodhāḥ śīlavāñ śuciḥ
english: Victory is certain for a king, and heaven follows thereafter, whose chief priest is learned in dharma, eloquent, of noble character, and pure.

sanskrit: lābhaṃ labdhum alabdhaṃ hi labdhaṃ ca parirakṣitum purohitaṃ prakurvīta rājā guṇasamanvitam
english: To gain what has not yet been gained, and to protect what has already been gained, a king should appoint a purohita endowed with virtuous qualities.

sanskrit: purohitamate tiṣṭhed ya icchet pṛthivīṃ nṛpaḥ prāptuṃ meruvarottaṃsāṃ sarvaśaḥ sāgarāmbarām
english: A king who wishes to obtain this entire earth, adorned by Meru as its crest jewel and girdled in all directions by ocean, should abide by the counsel of his purohita.

sanskrit: na hi kevalaśauryeṇa tāpatyābhijanena ca jayed abrāhmaṇaḥ kaś cid bhūmiṃ bhūmipatiḥ kva cit
english: For no king, lacking brahmin support, can ever conquer the earth by valor alone or by noble birth alone — not anywhere.

sanskrit: tasmād evaṃ vijānīhi kurūṇāṃ vaṃśavardhana brāhmaṇapramukhaṃ rājyaṃ śakyaṃ pālayituṃ ciram
english: Therefore understand this, O increaser of the Kuru lineage: a kingdom with brahmins at its head is alone capable of being sustained for a long time.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca tāpatya iti yad vākyam uktavān asi mām iha tad ahaṃ jñātum icchāmi tāpatyārthaviniścayam
english: Arjuna said: The word 'Tapatya' that you have addressed to me here — I wish to understand the definitive meaning of 'Tapatya.'

sanskrit: tapatī nāma kā caiṣā tāpatyā yatkṛte vayam kaunteyā hi vayaṃ sādho tattvam icchāmi veditum
english: Who is this Tapatī on account of whom we are called Tapatyas? We are the sons of Kuntī, O good one — I wish to know the truth.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktaḥ sa gandharvaḥ kuntīputraṃ dhanaṃjayam viśrutāṃ triṣu lokeṣu śrāvayām āsa vai kathām
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed, the gandharva caused Dhanañjaya, the son of Kuntī, to hear a tale renowned throughout the three worlds.

sanskrit: gandharva uvāca hanta te kathayiṣyāmi kathām etāṃ manoramām yathāvad akhilāṃ pārtha dharmyāṃ dharmabhṛtāṃ vara
english: The gandharva said: Come then — I shall tell you this delightful tale in full and exactly as it happened, O Pārtha, O best of those who uphold dharma — a righteous tale.

sanskrit: uktavān asmi yena tvāṃ tāpatya iti yad vacaḥ tat te 'haṃ kathayiṣyāmi śṛṇuṣvaikamanā mama
english: The word by which I addressed you as 'Tapatya' — that I shall narrate to you now. Listen to me with an undivided mind.

sanskrit: ya eṣa divi dhiṣṇyena nākaṃ vyāpnoti tejasā etasya tapatī nāma babhūvāsadṛśī sutā
english: He who pervades heaven with his seat and pervades the sky with his radiance — to him was born a daughter named Tapatī, matchless in form.

sanskrit: vivasvato vai kaunteya sāvitryavarajā vibho viśrutā triṣu lokeṣu tapatī tapasā yutā
english: She was the daughter of Vivasvat, O son of Kuntī, the younger sister of Sāvitrī, O lord, renowned in the three worlds, and endowed with the heat of ascetic power.

sanskrit: na devī nāsurī caiva na yakṣī na ca rākṣasī nāpsarā na ca gandharvī tathārūpeṇa kā cana
english: She was not a goddess, nor an asuri, nor a yakshi, nor a rakshasi, nor an apsara, nor a gandharvi — no one possessed a form equal to hers.

sanskrit: suvibhaktānavadyāṅgī svasitāyatalocanā svācārā caiva sādhvī ca suveṣā caiva bhāminī
english: Her limbs were well-proportioned and flawless; her eyes were dark and wide; she was virtuous in conduct, righteous, beautifully dressed, and resplendent.

sanskrit: na tasyāḥ sadṛśaṃ kaṃ cit triṣu lokeṣu bhārata bhartāraṃ savitā mene rūpaśīlakulaśrutaiḥ
english: Savitar found no one in the three worlds equal to her, O Bhārata — no one worthy to be her husband in beauty, character, lineage, and learning.

sanskrit: saṃprāptayauvanāṃ paśyan deyāṃ duhitaraṃ tu tām nopalebhe tataḥ śāntiṃ saṃpradānaṃ vicintayan
english: Seeing his daughter who had reached the bloom of youth, ready to be given in marriage, he found no peace as he pondered to whom to bestow her.

sanskrit: artharkṣaputraḥ kaunteya kurūṇām ṛṣabho balī sūryam ārādhayām āsa nṛpaḥ saṃvaraṇaḥ sadā
english: The son of Riksha and Artha, O son of Kuntī — Saṃvaraṇa, the bull among the Kurus, powerful king — always worshipped the Sun.

sanskrit: arghyamālyopahāraiś ca śaśvac ca nṛpatir yataḥ niyamair upavāsaiś ca tapobhir vividhair api
english: The king, ever steadfast, worshipped with offerings of water and garlands, with vows, fasts, and various austerities.

sanskrit: śuśrūṣur anahaṃvādī śuciḥ pauravanandanaḥ aṃśumantaṃ samudyantaṃ pūjayām āsa bhaktimān
english: Devoted in service, free of arrogance, pure — the joy of the Paurava clan — he worshipped with devotion the radiant one rising with his rays.

sanskrit: tataḥ kṛtajñaṃ dharmajñaṃ rūpeṇāsadṛśaṃ bhuvi tapatyāḥ sadṛśaṃ mene sūryaḥ saṃvaraṇaṃ patim
english: Then the Sun regarded Saṃvaraṇa — grateful, learned in dharma, matchless in form on earth — as a worthy husband for Tapatī.

sanskrit: dātum aicchat tataḥ kanyāṃ tasmai saṃvaraṇāya tām nṛpottamāya kauravya viśrutābhijanāya vai
english: He then wished to give his daughter to that Saṃvaraṇa, O Kauravya — that foremost of kings, of illustrious lineage.

sanskrit: yathā hi divi dīptāṃśuḥ prabhāsayati tejasā tathā bhuvi mahīpālo dīptyā saṃvaraṇo 'bhavat
english: Just as the bright-rayed sun illumines the sky with his radiance, so did Saṃvaraṇa shine upon the earth with his own brilliance.

sanskrit: yathārcayanti cādityam udyantaṃ brahmavādinaḥ tathā saṃvaraṇaṃ pārtha brāhmaṇāvarajāḥ prajāḥ
english: Just as the knowers of Brahman worship the rising Āditya, so did the people — brahmins and lower orders alike — worship Saṃvaraṇa, O Pārtha.

sanskrit: sa somam ati kāntatvād ādityam ati tejasā babhūva nṛpatiḥ śrīmān suhṛdāṃ durhṛdām api
english: That glorious king surpassed the moon in beauty and the sun in radiance — even in the eyes of enemies, not only of friends.

sanskrit: evaṃguṇasya nṛpates tathāvṛttasya kaurava tasmai dātuṃ manaś cakre tapatīṃ tapanaḥ svayam
english: For a king of such qualities and such conduct, O Kauravya, the Sun himself resolved to give Tapatī.

sanskrit: sa kadā cid atho rājā śrīmān uruyaśā bhuvi cacāra mṛgayāṃ pārtha parvatopavane kila
english: Then one day that glorious king, of wide renown upon the earth, went hunting, O Pārtha, in the forest on a mountain — so it is said.

sanskrit: carato mṛgayāṃ tasya kṣutpipāsāśramānvitaḥ mamāra rājñaḥ kaunteya girāv apratimo hayaḥ
english: As he ranged in the hunt, his peerless horse — worn out by hunger, thirst, and fatigue — died on the mountain, O son of Kuntī.

sanskrit: sa mṛtāśvaś caran pārtha padbhyām eva girau nṛpaḥ dadarśāsadṛśīṃ loke kanyām āyatalocanām
english: His horse dead, the king wandered on the mountain on foot alone, O Pārtha, and he saw a maiden with wide eyes, matchless in the world.

sanskrit: sa eka ekām āsādya kanyāṃ tām arimardanaḥ tasthau nṛpatiśārdūlaḥ paśyann avicalekṣaṇaḥ
english: He, the crusher of enemies, the tiger among kings, approaching that solitary maiden alone, stood still, gazing at her with unblinking eyes.

sanskrit: sa hi tāṃ tarkayām āsa rūpato nṛpatiḥ śriyam punaḥ saṃtarkayām āsa raver bhraṣṭām iva prabhām
english: The king surmised her to be Śrī herself in form, then surmised again that she was like the radiance of the sun fallen to earth.
